title: 1987–88 National Hurling League
text:
{{Short description|57th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1987–88 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 11 October 1987 – 29 July 1988 |teams = |team1 = Tipperary |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 15th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |oneb = |two = Offaly |three = Meath |four = Longford |previous = [[1986–87 National Hurling League|1986–87]] |next = [[1988–89 National Hurling League|1988–89]] }} The '''1987–88 National Hurling League''' (known as the '''[[Royal Liver Assurance|Royal Liver]] National Hurling League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 57th edition of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1987-88 |winners=[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]
15th National League title
Captain: [[Pat O'Neill (Tipperary hurler)|Pat O'Neill]]
Manager: [[Babs Keating|Michael Keating]] |relegated=[[Clare GAA|Clare]]
[[Cork GAA|Cork]] |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer=[[File: Colours of Tipperary.svg|border|20px]] [[Pat Fox]] (6-40) |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= 34 |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1986-87 National Hurling League|1986-87]] |nextseason=[[1988-89 National Hurling League|1988-89]] |updated=24 February 2017 }} [[Galway GAA|Galway]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1985-86 National Hurling League|1985-86 season]]. [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] entered Division 1 as the promoted teams. On 24 April 1988, [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] won the title following a 3-15 to 2-9 win over [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in the final. It was their first league title since [[1978-79 National Hurling League|1978-79]] and their 14th National League title overall.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}} [[Clare GAA|Clare]] and [[Cork GAA|Cork]] were relegated from Division 1.
